summary: First full E2E run (backend pytest 36 tests + Playwright UI on desktop 1920 and mobile 390). Core flows work end-to-end: storefront (MM/EN, dark mode, catalog filters, promotions, product detail with variants), Telegram deep-link checkout, Messenger order ref + copy + track, Telegram webhook simulation (secret 403, duplicate update_id, /start token, c:<intent> -> WEBSITE_TELEGRAM AWAITING_PAYMENT order, non-owner a:approve_yes refused + audited), admin login/lockout, product CRUD/promo validation/bulk/image upload/CSV import, supplier framework (SSRF blocks, masked key, validate/test/sync 4 items, DEMO-3 stock 0 -> out of stock, import + price_locked respected on re-sync, sync history), KBZPay enable validation, full order state machine via admin UI (evidence -> reject -> evidence -> approve (idempotent) -> manual deliver -> confirm -> complete, artifact purged 410), RBAC (CS 403 on approve/deliver/products/suppliers, UI shows no-approve-permission; PM 403 on orders; deactivated user tokens revoked), dashboard revenue = COMPLETED only, audit log, OG/sitemap/robots. 32/36 backend tests pass; the 4 failures are real findings (XFF lockout bypass, sitemap/OG host mismatch, CSV multi-plan rows not grouped, reject without note allowed). One confirmed UI logic bug on Order detail ('Customer confirmed' button shown in payment-review states).

critical.endpoint: core.client_ip (used by /api/auth/login lockout, /api/checkout/* and /api/orders/track rate limits)
critical.issue: Uses the FIRST X-Forwarded-For value, which is client-controlled (ingress appends the real IP). After 5 failed logins (429), the same email immediately returns 401 again when the request sends 'X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.4.4' -> brute-force lockout and checkout rate limit are trivially bypassable. Use the last (ingress-appended) hop / a trusted-proxy count instead.

minor.issue: Point to https://629dddf4-...preview.emergentagent.com while the current app URL (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL) is https://dav-ai-store--1vf4dwgp.preview.emergentagent.com. sitemap.xml <loc>, OG og:url/canonical, and Telegram webhook registration all use the old host; CORS ORIGINS also only contains the old host. Old host currently still responds so things work, but this must be updated/derived per environment before deploy.
Rejection reason is not required server-side (note='' -> 200). The UI shows a 'Reason / note' textarea but also does not enforce it. The Telegram customer then gets 'Reason: -'.

Each CSV row creates a separate product; rows with the same name but different plan/duration (e.g. 'X,1 Month' and 'X,1 Year') create 2 products with 1 plan each instead of 1 product with 2 plans. Also brand/category lookup uses an unescaped regex (f'^{name}$') -> names like 'C++' or '(Pro)' break or mis-match; use re.escape.

After lock expires the count stays >=5 and each new failure re-locks immediately for 15 min (count never resets on expiry). Also refresh endpoint issues new tokens without checking the user is still active (access tokens are checked on use, so impact is low).
'Confirm manual delivery' (to DELIVERED) is allowed directly from PAID_AWAITING_FULFILLMENT without any delivery artifact being recorded. Consider requiring a deliveries record or explicit note.
DNS is resolved in check_url and again by httpx (TOCTOU / DNS rebinding). Low risk; pin resolved IP or use a transport that validates the connected address.
Revenue is bucketed by order created_at rather than completed_at/paid_at; an order created before the window but completed inside it is excluded.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Customer confirmed' button (to AWAITING_PAYMENT) renders whenever AWAITING_PAYMENT is an allowed transition, i.e. also in PAYMENT_SUBMITTED / PAYMENT_UNDER_REVIEW / PAYMENT_REJECTED. Clicking it in review states actually triggers request_more_evidence (no note) and messages the customer. It also duplicates data-testid 'action-awaiting_payment' with 'Request more evidence'. Restrict to s in {CHECKOUT_STARTED, AWAITING_CUSTOMER_CONFIRMATION} and give unique testids.

set() builds from the render-time 'sp' closure (new URLSearchParams(sp)). Two filter changes in quick succession (or the 350ms debounced search firing after another filter change) overwrite each other; e.g. clearing min and max price quickly left min_price=20000 in the URL. Use setSp(prev => {...}) functional updates.

No client-side route guard by permission: a customer_service user can open /admin/products and /admin/suppliers directly and sees the page shell with 'Import CSV/XLSX' and 'New product' buttons (API correctly returns 403). Redirect or show a 'no permission' state.

rca of the issue: XFF bypass: core.client_ip returns request.headers['x-forwarded-for'].split(',')[0]; Kubernetes ingress appends the real client IP to any client-supplied XFF, so element [0] is attacker-controlled. Repro: 5 failed logins for an email -> 429; 6th with header X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.4.4 -> 401 (attempt counted under a new identifier). Mitigation: use the right-most untrusted hop (e.g. split(',')[-1]) or configure a trusted proxy count. 'Customer confirmed' bug: OrderDetail.jsx line 82 calls A('Customer confirmed','AWAITING_PAYMENT') unconditionally; TRANSITIONS for PAYMENT_SUBMITTED include AWAITING_PAYMENT, so the button appears and maps to request_more_evidence on the backend.
